result.timing:
Measured on this machine with the harness, test executable run directly, Release build without analyzers or warnings as errors.
- One worker, killed mutant: build 3.6 to 5.4 s, first filter 7 to 25 s, 11 to 37 s end to end (mean 24 s, including the rerun that confirms a kill by one or two failing tests).
- One worker, survivor PFR-1426 (R13a's C5): build 5.4 s, first filter 24.6 s (3487 tests), whole suite 199 s (10970 tests). 229 s in all.
- Whole suite alone on an unmutated build: 166 s. The rest of the suite after a first filter, at 2 workers: 150 to 190 s.
- Parallelism, the same 16 mutants each time:
  - 4 workers: 27.1 s per mutant, 8.8 mutants a minute.
  - 8 workers: 44.7 s per mutant (build 10.6 s, first filter 31.2 s), 10.7 a minute.
  - 12 workers: 70.4 s per mutant (build 18 s, first filter 48 s), 10.2 a minute.
- 12 is past the peak, so I lowered the run to 8 workers: at most 4 agents of 2 workers each.
- 8 workers with --stop-on-fail: 21.5 s per mutant, 22 a minute.
- Estimate at 8 workers with full failure counts: 239324 worker-seconds, about 8.3 h of wall clock, or about 8.5 to 9 h if shards are handed out in waves of 4 (27 shards of 63 to 81 min at 2 workers). The model assumes 8 percent of mutants survive the first filter and need 300 s for the rest of the suite; that part is about a third of the total.
- The same estimate with --stop-on-fail: about 5.6 h.
- Caveat: some timing runs overlapped the final pass's own runs and a .NET update, so per-mutant numbers may be somewhat high.

problems: The step is feasible but long. 3736 mutants take about 8.3 h of wall clock at the best parallelism I measured (8 workers; 12 was slower than 8). That is still within ADR 53's bound, since the review took longer. The smallest change that roughly halves the first pass is to run with --stop-on-fail, which gives about 5.6 h, but each kill's failure count becomes a floor. Another option is to run every shard with --first-only and then give the SURVIVED-FIRST ids the rest of the suite in a second phase.
The task's 6 agents of 2 workers (12 builds) is past the peak: throughput was 10.2 mutants a minute against 10.7 at 8 workers. I sized the run for at most 4 agents of 2 workers.

I generate ADR 53's literal catalog:
- false for whole conditions and alternatives, true for whole conditions and conjuncts. A conjunct's false and an alternative's true would repeat the whole condition's.
- Constant bounds +1 and -1, including char bounds in range calls and comparisons.
- No shifts of non-constant expressions such as candidate + 1. Earlier stages ran those, and 126 of their records fall outside this catalog.
